resources.string: Import your own word lists. The keyboard then completes and corrects words that it does not ship with. Most languages have no bundled word list. For those languages, the lists here give the suggestions. You can import a list, or download one from Settings → Languages. If the app bundles a list, your lists add to it.\n\nFormat: one word for each line. You can add a space and a frequency number after the word. The keyboard ignores lines that start with #. Autocorrect never changes a word that you import.
Delete the word list %1$s
Use only my word lists
Turn off the bundled and downloaded word lists for this language

Your imported lists usually add to the words the keyboard already has. Turn this on and the keyboard forgets those words for this language and reads your lists only. Use it when the bundled list or a downloaded list suggests words that you do not want. Suggestions, autocorrect and glide typing all follow this setting. Words that you teach the keyboard as you type are kept. This setting is for one language. It changes nothing for your other languages.
No word list is on for this language, so the keyboard has no words to suggest. Turn on a list above, import one, or turn this setting off.

Emoji search includes English and Bengali keywords. A pack adds one more language. Then %1$s all find 💰. The words of the pack also show as emoji suggestions while you type.\n\nA pack adds to the bundled keywords. It does not replace them. One language can have more than one pack.
Downloads
Download automatically
Download keywords for the languages that you type

When you turn a language on, the app downloads its emoji keywords in the background. This is about 100 KB, one time. If you turn this off, the Download buttons below are the only way to get the keywords.
Delete the emoji pack %1$s
Import pack

Import format: a file with tab separators. Put one emoji on each line, then a tab, then the keywords with comma separators. You can add one more tab and a display name. The app ignores lines that start with \"# \". The JSON emoji dictionaries from the wmkeyboard-data repository import as they are.
Load an emoji pack from a URL
A link to an emoji keyword file with tab separators
The app found no emoji in that file. Make sure that it is a keyword pack.
